modules.src:
###
Time correlation functions of a trajectory and the diffusion coefficient
they give: the velocity autocorrelation function <v(0) . v(t)>, the
mean-square displacement <|r(t) - r(0)|^2> and the cross-correlation
<v(0) . (r(t) - r(0))>, each averaged over atoms and over time origins
spaced along the trajectory. Positions are unfolded across the periodic
boundaries frame by frame. By the Green-Kubo and Einstein relations,

    D = (1/3) int_0^inf <v(0) . v(t)> dt = lim (1/6) d<|r(t) - r(0)|^2>/dt.

This is diffusion of Allen and Tildesley's examples for Computer
Simulation of Liquids (2nd ed., Oxford University Press, 2017;
https://github.com/Allen-Tildesley/examples), ported to Viv. Upstream reads
the frames from files cnf.000, cnf.001, ...; here they come as arrays. The
two estimates of D are this port's addition.
###
# The program behind `vp.liquids.diffusion` (diffusion.export.toml).
#
#     viv run ports/liquids/diffusion.viv
#
# Derived from diffusion.f90 of https://github.com/Allen-Tildesley/examples
# (commit 4818bc82), by Michael P. Allen and Dominic J. Tildesley, CC0-1.0;
# see ports/liquids/LICENSE.
from ports.liquids.setup import DIM
from ports.liquids.analysis import correlations, correlations_add, correlations_result, diffusion_coefficients

#| The default trajectory: two atoms crossing the box at constant velocities
#| (1, 0, 0) and (0, -1/2, 0), a frame every delta.
def ballistic_frames(nframes: Int, delta: Num, box: Num) {
    fr = zeros(2 * nframes, DIM)
    fv = zeros(2 * nframes, DIM)
    for t to nframes {
        fv[2 * t, 0] = 1.0
        fv[2 * t + 1, 1] = -0.5
        fr[2 * t, 0] = t * delta * fv[2 * t, 0]
        fr[2 * t + 1, 1] = t * delta * fv[2 * t + 1, 1]
    }
    return fr - box * round(fr / box), fv
}

#: n  the atoms in each frame
n: Int = 2
#: box  the box side, in sigma
box = 4.0
#: delta  the time between frames
delta = 0.05
#: frames_r  the positions of every frame one after another, (frames x n, 3), in sigma, each inside the box; by default two atoms crossing the box at constant velocity for 41 frames
#: frames_v  the velocities of every frame, the same shape
frames_r, frames_v = ballistic_frames(41, 0.05, 4.0)
#: nt  the functions run over 0 to nt frames apart
nt: Int = 20
#: origin_interval  a time origin every this many frames
origin_interval: Int = 5

nrows: Int = int(shape(frames_r)[0])
if int(shape(frames_v)[0]) != nrows or n < 1 or nrows % n != 0 {
    stop(f"frames_r and frames_v must have the same number of rows, a whole number of frames of n = {n} atoms")
}
nframes: Int = nrows // n
c = correlations(n, nt, origin_interval)
for t to nframes {
    correlations_add(c, frames_r[t * n:(t + 1) * n, :], frames_v[t * n:(t + 1) * n, :], box)
}
#: vacf  <v(0) . v(t)> per atom at 0 to nt frames apart
vacf = zeros(0)
#: rvcf  <v(0) . (r(t) - r(0))> per atom
rvcf = zeros(0)
#: msd  <|r(t) - r(0)|^2> per atom
msd = zeros(0)
vacf, rvcf, msd = correlations_result(c, n)
#: time  the times, 0 to nt delta
time = linspace(0.0, nt * delta, nt + 1)
#: d_vacf  D as one third of the integral of the VACF over the range (trapezoids)
d_vacf = 0.0
#: d_msd  D as one sixth of the slope of the MSD over the second half of the range (least squares)
d_msd = 0.0
d_vacf, d_msd = diffusion_coefficients(vacf, msd, delta)

print(f"{nframes} frames of {n} atoms; D from the VACF {fmt(d_vacf, '.6f')}, from the MSD {fmt(d_msd, '.6f')}")

test "the VACF at t = 0 is the mean square velocity" {
    s = 0.0
    for i to nrows {
        s += dot(frames_v[i, :], frames_v[i, :])
    }
    assert_near(vacf[0], s / nrows, 1.0e-12 * s / nrows)
}

modules.src:
###
What a simulation's configurations are used for after the run, as Allen
and Tildesley's analysis programs compute it:

- the pair distribution function g(r), from a histogram of pair
  separations over many configurations (pair_distribution.f90);
- the velocity autocorrelation function <v(0) . v(t)>, the mean-square
  displacement <|r(t) - r(0)|^2> and their cross-correlation
  <v(0) . (r(t) - r(0))>, over time origins spaced along a trajectory
  (diffusion.f90), and the diffusion coefficient that each gives;
- the statistical error of a time average when successive values are
  correlated, by block averaging (error_calc.f90).

The histogram and the correlation functions accumulate one configuration
at a time, so a simulation can feed them as it runs instead of writing the
configurations out.
###
# Derived from pair_distribution.f90, diffusion.f90 and error_calc.f90 of
# https://github.com/Allen-Tildesley/examples (commit 4818bc82), by Michael P.
# Allen and Dominic J. Tildesley, CC0-1.0; see ports/liquids/LICENSE. The
# diffusion coefficients from the curves (diffusion_coefficients) are this
# port's; upstream leaves that step to the reader.

# ---- g(r)

from setup import DIM

#| A g(r) histogram: counts[k] pairs (each counted twice, i-j and j-i) with
#| separation in [k dr, (k + 1) dr), frames[0] configurations so far, the
#| bin width dr in box units.
record PairHistogram {
    counts: [Int]
    frames: [Int]
    dr: Num
}

#| An empty histogram for bins of width dr (in sigma) out to half the box.
def pair_histogram(dr: Num, box: Num) -> PairHistogram {
    dr_box = dr / box
    nk: Int = int(floor(0.5 / dr_box))
    return PairHistogram { counts: int_zeros(nk), frames: int_zeros(1), dr: dr_box }
}

#| Adds one configuration (n, 3), positions in sigma, to the histogram.
def pair_add(h: PairHistogram, frame: Arr, box: Num) {
    nat: Int = int(shape(frame)[0])
    nk: Int = len(h.counts)
    r = frame / box
    for i to nat - 1 {
        for j from i + 1 to nat {
            dx = r[i, 0] - r[j, 0]
            dy = r[i, 1] - r[j, 1]
            dz = r[i, 2] - r[j, 2]
            dx = dx - round(dx)
            dy = dy - round(dy)
            dz = dz - round(dz)
            rij_sq = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz
            k: Int = int(floor(sqrt(rij_sq) / h.dr))
            if k < nk {
                h.counts[k] += 2
            }
        }
    }
    h.frames[0] += 1
}

#| g(r) at the bins' midpoints (in sigma) for n atoms: each bin's count
#| per atom and per frame over the count an ideal gas of the same density
#| would give, (4 pi rho / 3) (r_hi^3 - r_lo^3), in box units where rho = n.
def pair_g(h: PairHistogram, nat: Int, box: Num) {
    nk: Int = len(h.counts)
    const = 4.0 * pi * nat / 3.0
    g = zeros(nk)
    rmid = zeros(nk)
    for k to nk {
        g[k] = 1.0 * h.counts[k] / (1.0 * nat * h.frames[0])
        r_lo = 1.0 * k * h.dr
        r_hi = r_lo + h.dr
        h_id = const * (r_hi * r_hi * r_hi - r_lo * r_lo * r_lo)
        g[k] = g[k] / h_id
        rmid[k] = (k + 1.0 - 0.5) * (h.dr * box)
    }
    return rmid, g
}

# ---- time correlation functions

#| The accumulators of diffusion.f90: n0 time origins kept in a ring, each
#| origin's positions and velocities, the sums of msd, rvcf and vacf at each
#| separation 0 to nt (in frames) and how many origin pairs went into each,
#| the previous frame (to unfold the periodic boundaries), and the counters
#| [frame number t, ring slot mk, ring full (0 or 1)].
record Correlations {
    nt: Int
    origin_interval: Int
    t0: [Int]
    r0: Arr
    v0: Arr
    r_old: Arr
    msd: Arr
    rvcf: Arr
    vacf: Arr
    norm: Arr
    counters: [Int]
}

T_FRAME: Int = 0
MK: Int = 1
FULL: Int = 2

#| Accumulators for n atoms, separations up to nt frames, an origin every
#| origin_interval frames.
def correlations(nat: Int, nt: Int, origin_interval: Int) -> Correlations {
    n0: Int = nt // origin_interval + 1
    return Correlations { nt: nt, origin_interval: origin_interval, t0: int_zeros(n0), r0: zeros(n0 * nat, DIM),
                          v0: zeros(n0 * nat, DIM), r_old: zeros(nat, DIM), msd: zeros(nt + 1), rvcf: zeros(nt + 1),
                          vacf: zeros(nt + 1), norm: zeros(nt + 1), counters: int_zeros(DIM) }
}

#| Adds the next frame of a trajectory: positions (n, 3) in sigma as the
#| simulation keeps them (inside the box) and velocities. Positions are
#| unfolded against the previous frame, so an atom that crossed the box
#| edge keeps its true displacement.
def correlations_add(c: Correlations, frame_r: Arr, frame_v: Arr, box: Num) {
    nat: Int = int(shape(frame_r)[0])
    n0: Int = len(c.t0)
    t: Int = c.counters[T_FRAME]
    r = copy(frame_r)
    if t > 0 {
        for i to nat {
            for k to DIM {
                r[i, k] = r[i, k] - c.r_old[i, k]
                r[i, k] = r[i, k] - round(r[i, k] / box) * box
                r[i, k] = r[i, k] + c.r_old[i, k]
            }
        }
    }
    if t % c.origin_interval == 0 {
        mk: Int = c.counters[MK] + 1
        if mk > n0 {
            c.counters[FULL] = 1
            mk = mk - n0
        }
        c.counters[MK] = mk
        c.t0[mk - 1] = t
        for i to nat {
            for k to DIM {
                c.r0[(mk - 1) * nat + i, k] = r[i, k]
                c.v0[(mk - 1) * nat + i, k] = frame_v[i, k]
            }
        }
    }
    nk: Int = c.counters[MK]
    if c.counters[FULL] == 1 {
        nk = n0
    }
    for o to nk {
        dt: Int = t - c.t0[o]
        if dt <= c.nt {
            s_msd = 0.0
            s_rv = 0.0
            s_vv = 0.0
            for i to nat {
                for k to DIM {
                    d = r[i, k] - c.r0[o * nat + i, k]
                    s_msd += d * d
                    s_rv += d * c.v0[o * nat + i, k]
                    s_vv += frame_v[i, k] * c.v0[o * nat + i, k]
                }
            }
            c.msd[dt] = c.msd[dt] + s_msd
            c.rvcf[dt] = c.rvcf[dt] + s_rv
            c.vacf[dt] = c.vacf[dt] + s_vv
            c.norm[dt] = c.norm[dt] + 1.0
        }
    }
    for i to nat {
        for k to DIM {
            c.r_old[i, k] = r[i, k]
        }
    }
    c.counters[T_FRAME] = t + 1
}

#| The averaged functions per atom at separations 0 to nt frames: vacf,
#| rvcf and msd (upstream's diffusion.out columns 2 to 4).
def correlations_result(c: Correlations, nat: Int) {
    vacf = c.vacf / c.norm / (1.0 * nat)
    rvcf = c.rvcf / c.norm / (1.0 * nat)
    msd = c.msd / c.norm / (1.0 * nat)
    return vacf, rvcf, msd
}

#| The diffusion coefficient two ways, from curves sampled every delta in
#| time: one third of the integral of the VACF (trapezoids over the whole
#| range), and one sixth of the slope of the MSD, a least-squares line
#| through its second half. They agree when the range is long enough for
#| the VACF to have decayed and the MSD to have become linear.
def diffusion_coefficients(vacf: Arr, msd: Arr, delta: Num) {
    m: Int = len(vacf)
    integral = 0.0
    for k from 1 to m {
        integral += 0.5 * (vacf[k - 1] + vacf[k]) * delta
    }
    k0: Int = (m - 1) // 2
    np = 1.0 * (m - k0)
    st = 0.0
    sy = 0.0
    for k from k0 to m {
        st += k * delta
        sy += msd[k]
    }
    tbar = st / np
    ybar = sy / np
    sxy = 0.0
    sxx = 0.0
    for k from k0 to m {
        sxy += (k * delta - tbar) * (msd[k] - ybar)
        sxx += (k * delta - tbar) * (k * delta - tbar)
    }
    return integral / 3.0, sxy / sxx / 6.0
}

# ---- errors of correlated averages (error_calc.f90)

#| Block analysis of a series a(1..m), two ways, as error_calc.f90 does
#| after its run:
#|  - for nblock = 20 down to 4 blocks, the standard error of the mean from
#|    the scatter of the block means;
#|  - by repeated halving (Flyvbjerg and Petersen): the series is averaged
#|    in pairs again and again, and after each halving the naive error of
#|    the shorter series is computed.
#| Each estimate comes with the statistical inefficiency s = tblock
#| var(block means) / var(a), which levels off at 2 tau (tau the
#| correlation time in steps) once blocks are long enough; the error is
#| then sqrt(s var(a) / m). Returns the mean, the sample variance, the
#| naive error, then for each method the block lengths, the errors and s.
def blocking(series: Arr) {
    m: Int = len(series)
    max_blocks: Int = 20
    min_blocks: Int = 4
    mean_a = 0.0
    for t to m {
        mean_a += series[t]
    }
    mean_a = mean_a / m
    a = series - mean_a
    var_1 = 0.0
    for t to m {
        var_1 += a[t] * a[t]
    }
    var_1 = var_1 / (m - 1)
    err_naive = sqrt(var_1 / m)
    nb_fixed: Int = max_blocks - min_blocks + 1
    t_fixed = zeros(nb_fixed)
    e_fixed = zeros(nb_fixed)
    s_fixed = zeros(nb_fixed)
    for q to nb_fixed {
        nblock: Int = max_blocks - q
        tblock: Int = m // nblock
        trun: Int = nblock * tblock
        a_run = 0.0
        for t to trun {
            a_run += a[t]
        }
        a_run = a_run / trun
        a_var = 0.0
        for blk to nblock {
            a_blk = 0.0
            for t from blk * tblock to (blk + 1) * tblock {
                a_blk += a[t] - a_run
            }
            a_blk = a_blk / tblock
            a_var = a_var + a_blk * a_blk
        }
        a_var = a_var / (nblock - 1)
        t_fixed[q] = 1.0 * tblock
        e_fixed[q] = sqrt(a_var / nblock)
        s_fixed[q] = tblock * a_var / var_1
    }
    t_half = zeros(0)
    e_half = zeros(0)
    s_half = zeros(0)
    b = copy(a)
    nblock: Int = m
    tblock: Int = 1
    nblock = nblock // 2
    tblock = tblock * 2
    while nblock >= 3 {
        for t to nblock {
            b[t] = (b[2 * t] + b[2 * t + 1]) / 2.0
        }
        b_avg = 0.0
        for t to nblock {
            b_avg += b[t]
        }
        b_avg = b_avg / nblock
        b_var = 0.0
        for t to nblock {
            b[t] = b[t] - b_avg
            b_var += b[t] * b[t]
        }
        b_var = b_var / (nblock - 1)
        t_half = append(t_half, 1.0 * tblock)
        e_half = append(e_half, sqrt(b_var / nblock))
        s_half = append(s_half, tblock * b_var / var_1)
        nblock = nblock // 2
        tblock = tblock * 2
    }
    return mean_a, var_1, err_naive, t_fixed, e_fixed, s_fixed, t_half, e_half, s_half
}

test "g(r) of points spread uniformly is 1 within its noise" {
    srand(3.0)
    nat: Int = 200
    box = 10.0
    nframes: Int = 20
    h = pair_histogram(0.5, box)
    for fr to nframes {
        x = (rand(nat, 3) - 0.5) * box
        pair_add(h, x, box)
    }
    rmid, g = pair_g(h, nat, box)
    assert_near(rmid[0], 0.25, 1.0e-12)
    last = len(g) - 1
    assert_near(g[last], 1.0, 0.05)
}

test "atoms moving at constant velocity: msd = |v|^2 t^2, vacf = |v|^2, rvcf = |v|^2 t" {
    nat: Int = 4
    box = 5.0
    v = [[0.3, 0.0, 0.0], [0.0, -0.2, 0.0], [0.1, 0.1, 0.1], [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]]
    nt: Int = 20
    nsteps: Int = 3 * nt
    c = correlations(nat, nt, 5)
    r = zeros(nat, DIM)
    for t to nsteps {
        x = r + v * t
        x = x - box * round(x / box)
        correlations_add(c, x, v, box)
    }
    vacf, rvcf, msd = correlations_result(c, nat)
    v2 = sum(v * v) / nat
    assert_near(vacf[7], v2, 1.0e-14)
    assert_near(rvcf[7], 7.0 * v2, 1.0e-12)
    assert_near(msd[20], 400.0 * v2, 1.0e-10)
}

test "blocking an uncorrelated series gives s near 1" {
    srand(11.0)
    a = rand(4096)
    mean_a, var_1, err_naive, t_fixed, e_fixed, s_fixed, t_half, e_half, s_half = blocking(a)
    assert_near(var_1, 1.0 / 12.0, 0.01)
    assert_near(s_half[2], 1.0, 0.5)
}
